neighbours.label: ' Super', ' super' or ' Hyper' in technical words and names (Super|computing, super|conductor, Hyper|Threading, Hyper|-V), weaker in everyday uses (Super Bowl), as opposed to other technical words in the same frames
fire: The lab runs a Cray supercomputer for weather models.
The Barcelona Supercomputing Center opened in 2005.
The new superconductor works at higher temperatures.
Intel HyperThreading doubles the number of threads.
We run Hyper-V on the old server in the basement.
The critics used every superlative they could find.
The SuperCollider software makes sound from code.
The HyperCard program was popular on old Macs.
quiet: The lab runs a Cray mainframe for weather models.
The Barcelona Computing Center opened in 2005.
The new semiconductor works at higher temperatures.
Intel MultiThreading doubles the number of threads.
We run VirtualBox on the old server in the basement.
The critics used every adjective they could find.
The Super Bowl drew a large crowd last year.
My Super Nintendo sits in the attic with old Macs.

short: Super- or Hyper- in technical words and names
notes: Card: ' Super' x12, ' super' x10, ' Hyper' x3, 'SUPER', 'Super', ' Gig'. Output promotes ' fifth', ' next', 'Seventh', not explained. Probes: ' Hyper' 0.34-0.96, ' Super' in Supercomputing 0.62-0.74, ' super' 0.33-0.53; Ultra 0.06, Micro 0.01, 'Computing' 0.20, Mega 0.20. Less clear: Super Bowl 0.30, 'super nice' 0.28, Superman 0.26, hypermarket 0.28, Super Mario 0.14, superhero 0.05, so non-technical uses are lower but not silent. The declared tokens include those uses, so coverage is an upper bound.
